headline: UK AI Security Institute questions what simulated sabotage tests prove
body: A UK AI Security Institute study questions what simulated sabotage tests prove about AI agent monitors. Its case study is a GPT-5.4 monitor that OpenAI previously used in production. It missed just 0.2 to 0.5 percent of harmful actions under standard attacks, but better-optimized attacks pushed that miss rate as high as 23 percent.
note: The study's point is that simulated attacks alone can't show a monitor will hold up in live use, a question for any bank letting AI agents act on its systems.

evidence.text: AI companies including OpenAI and Anthropic test them with simulated sabotage attempts.
A new study from the UK AI Security Institute calls into question what those tests actually prove.
As a case study, the researchers examined a monitoring system built on GPT-5.4 that OpenAI previously used in production.
Against standard attacks, the monitor missed just 0.2 to 0.5 percent of harmful actions.
Better-optimized attacks pushed that false-negative rate as high as 23 percent.
Simulated attack tests alone can't show that an AI monitor will hold up in live use, and the industry hasn't made a solid case yet that such tests reflect real-world safety, the study concludes.
AI companies including OpenAI and Anthropic use these tests to evaluate automated monitors for AI agents.
